# Implementation Plans

Two tracks live here.

**001 — remediation.** Generated by the improve skill on 2026-08-09, audited
against commit `e773b65`. By request, the entire audit was consolidated into a
**single plan** rather than one plan per finding. Execute its Parts in order —
they are sequenced so the codebase is never broken between Parts, and each Part
commits independently so a failing one can be reverted without losing the others.

**002–006 — the ideas.** [`002-ideas.md`](002-ideas.md) is the raw input;
[`002-review.md`](002-review.md) is the verdict layer (what each idea is really
asking for, what it costs, build or not) and routes to the four plans below.
Read 002-review first — it carries the benchmarks and the reasoning that two of
the four verdicts rest on.

Read a plan fully before starting, honor its STOP conditions, and update the
status row when done.

### 001 — what landed, and what it left open

All 16 Parts landed across 19 commits on `advisor/001-audit-remediation`.
Build and typecheck are clean with the new flags on; the suite went 338 → 394.
Four things a reader should not have to rediscover:

- **Part 13d's digests are empty.** The verification path is built, wired and
  tested, but no model in `WHISPER_MODELS` declares a `sha256`, so every model
  download is still unverified. Fetching them needs the network and gigabytes.
  This is the plan's own sanctioned fallback, not an oversight — but the
  protection is inert until somebody fills them in.
- **Part 14d was not done.** The cache still stores the full entry per path and
  `persist()` still rewrites the whole file on every write. What landed under
  that heading is 14b's memoisation plus a correctness fix: an entry whose
  frontmatter holds a value JSON cannot carry is no longer cached at all,
  because a warm cache was silently deleting those keys from the user's file
  (I1 and I3). Trimming the format is still open, and is the prerequisite
  question [005](005-mac-app.md) raises.
- **The repository URL is unverified.** `https://github.com/yosefserkez/ppr` is
  now in both manifests and three READMEs. It was supplied directly rather than
  read from a remote — this repo still has none configured.
- **Two things the plan's scope list did not anticipate.** `search.ts` gained a
  filter mode (Part 9: routing the browse filter through `searchEntries`
  unmodified turned it from AND into OR and blanked the pane on the first
  keystroke), and `types.ts`/`util/id.ts`/`util/order.ts`/`ai/*.ts` were needed
  by Parts 4 and 8 as written. `plugins.ts` and `setup/checks.ts` were needed to
  finish 13b and 13d. The scope list was incomplete, not the work.

## Dependency notes (within 001)

- Part 1 must land before any Part that adds tests (2–15), or a green run tests
  the stale build.
- Parts 4 (11) and (12) are entangled — both destroy an adopted file's id — and
  are handled together within Part 4.
- Parts 2+ (SECURITY-01/-02/-08) share one fix locus (`loadConfig` +
  `deepMerge`) and are one Part on purpose.
- Every other Part is independent; reorder freely after Part 1 if needed.

## Direction findings (options for the maintainer, not scheduled work)

Not turned into plans — these are product decisions, recorded so they aren't lost:

- **`ppr-mcp` as a pull plugin** — an MCP server exposing `context`/`search`/`ask`
  over the existing `--json` surface; one file away given I13, and squarely on the
  "ppr feeds other AI tools" direction. Best as a design/spike plan when wanted.
- **`ppr import`** — the inverse of `export -f jsonl`, currently missing; the
  highest-value missing entry point for a tool whose rival is "a text file". Needs
  an id/dedup design before building. Plan 003 makes it *more* wanted (a day's
  report is an import) without making it necessary.

Added by the 002 review, in the same spirit:

- **`.ppr/state.json` is tracked and syncs.** `.gitignore` excludes
  `.ppr/cache/` but not the learner's high-water mark, and resolving a merge
  conflict on it the obvious way (take the higher id) skips entries permanently
  — L23's failure. Two lines and a test; see [006](006-cloud-sync.md) Part VI.
  Worth doing whether or not sync is ever built.
- **The index cache stores full entry bodies** — 8.2 MB at 6 000 entries,
  re-parsed on every command, and the reason cold start is 668 ms at that size.
  A recorded tradeoff for a CLI; a prerequisite question for [005](005-mac-app.md).
- **Retrieval degrades silently past 150 facts.** `FACTS_IN_PROMPT`
  (`core/src/vault.ts:127`) is where "send the whole store" stops being true,
  and `context()` with no query is uncapped. [004](004-tidy.md) is the
  maintenance answer; a one-line warning is the cheap one.

## Findings considered and rejected

- ESLint / Prettier / Biome: not added — would fight the hand-wrapped comment
  style AGENTS.md §6 mandates and mostly duplicate `tsc`; the only real gap is the
  unused-symbol check, done in Part 12 with zero new tooling. (DX-04)
- `Catalog.load()` re-stat, `Vault` facade size, lexical-only search,
  whole-fact-store-in-prompt, per-file temp+rename: recorded tradeoffs in AGENTS.md,
  by design.
- Deferred (lower leverage, not rejected): Screen/Keyboard stream seam (TESTS-03),
  model-derived-frontmatter validation (SECURITY-09), and removing the unused
  `graph()` export (DEBT-03 — a breaking `@ppr/core` API change, bundle it with a
  future API cleanup). Noted in Part 001's maintenance notes.
